label: Longer unit-output runs can favor replenishment over finite reserve by any prescribed factor
paraphrase: With both external feeds zero, an exact run of N unit-output intervals fits a natural-number initial reserve bound m exactly when N ≤ m. For any one fixed proper conditional distribution on the finite bounds, the prior mass of fitting bounds equals one minus the mass below N. Fix positive class priors, a stored-class likelihood between zero and that fitting mass at each N, and a supplied-class likelihood between a common positive lower bound and one. For every prescribed positive factor, all sufficiently long finite runs give the supplied account comparative posterior weight strictly greater than that factor times the stored account's weight. A fixed full-support geometric distribution on the finite bounds gives deterministic stored likelihood (1/2)^N, which is positive for every finite N. Under that control, at each fixed N and positive stored-class prior, no positive supplied weight is at least every positive factor times the stored weight.
